The East Texas salt structure province covers over eleven (11)
counties which includes Van Zandt County. There are approximately
seventeen 17 Oil and Gas bearing formation in Van Zandt County which
include: Nacatoch, Taylor, Pecan Gap, Austin, Eagle Ford, Woodbine,
Buda, Grayson, Georgetown, Fredericksburg, Paluxy, Glen Rose,
Rodessa, Pettet, Travis Peak, Cotton Valley and Smackover.
 
Any of these formations could be a potential trap for accumulating
migrating oil and gas. As illustrated in the nearby Quitman Field where
close drilling occurred, main and secondary faults can be accurately
defined. In this proposed Robinson #1 well, the act of well control
(number of wells) prevents such close control or mapping of these
faults and structures.
 
There are four (4) fields surrounding the Robinson #1: The Myrtle
Springs Field, Edgewood Field, Fruitvale East Field and the Fruitvale
Field. The Robinson #1 is considered an extension of the Fruitvale
Field. Faults that are created by the upward migration of the Louann
salt bed have cut through some if not all of the formation above this
salt and have created these four (4) surrounding fields as oil an gas
became trapped and accumulate. All of the salt domes in the East Texas
salt structure province have created dozens of field throughout the
province and these domes push upward in their migration toward the
surface. The probability of undiscovered trapped oil and gas within any
of these seventeen (17) plus formations is high due to this "under
drilling" of the Robinson lease.
 
This area is termed a "stacked"field with potential production
inmany, fi not all of the shallower formations. No one (1) formation
make up these four (4) fields; however, the Smackdown formation is
theformation that is sustained, and high production is the common
factor throughout.
